# Phase A grounding: forward a failing CI check to the owning worker

Repo: Go module "dispatch" at the current directory. Traced by three explorers (decision path, cache + GitHub, worker delivery + docs) and one source-control "why" investigator. Gaps: `gh` is not authenticated in the sandbox, so PR bodies/threads and ticket ENG-232 were not read; no Linear/Slack/Notion MCP was consulted; no `docs/adr/` and no `CONTEXT.md` exist. Tests were read only partly.

## Objective (approved)
When a check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide: extend the existing PR nudge or a separate rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## Architecture: pure planner + impure shell
- `internal/reconcile/reconcile.go`: `Plan(Input) []Action` is pure. `Input` carries tickets, `Workers`, `PRs` (map ticket -> `pullrequest.PR`), `Cache`, `NudgeLimit`. `Action{Kind, Ticket, Reason, PaneID, Text, Head}`. Kinds: Launch, Wait, Skip, Escalate, Nudge, Notify, Teardown, Stop, Keep, Promote, Close.
- `dispatch.go`: `tick` loads `cache.json`, snapshots workers (`worker.Find`: treehouse lease -> herdr workspace -> first `claude` agent; state None/Idle/Working/Blocked), calls `readPRs` (line ~332), `Plan`, `settle` (line 534, runs BEFORE actions), then executes actions, then `cache.Save` (atomic temp+rename; skipped on --dry-run). Default tick interval 5 minutes (`interval_minutes`).
- Tests are root-package `dispatch_test` files (`review_test.go`, `nudge_test.go`, `comment_test.go`, `ready_test.go`, `dispatch_test.go` harness with a fake `gh` at ~line 505 serving one JSON shape from `h.pr`, fake herdr). No `_test.go` inside `internal/reconcile`; planning is tested through `tick`.

## The existing PR nudge (`inReviewIdle`, reconcile.go:374-387)
```go
if ok && pr.Ready && prev.ReadyHead != pr.Head { return Notify ReasonReady }
if !ok || !pr.NeedsWork() { return Action{}, false }
nudges := prev.NudgesAt(t.Status, pr.Head)
if nudges >= in.NudgeLimit { return Escalate "its worker stayed idle through %d nudges about %s without pushing..." }
return Nudge{Reason: ReasonPR+": "+pr.Problem(), PaneID: w.PaneID, Text: fmt.Sprintf(PRNudge, pr.URL, t.Identifier, pr.Problem())}
```
- `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."` Fixed text; tests (`review_test.go:19`) hardcode it. "Fix it and push" was reworded because it made the worker skip step 7's claim-checking (decision-log line 127).
- It is NOT once per head. It is up to `NudgeLimit` (default 2, `nudge_limit`) nudges per (status, PR head), then Escalate to Needs Human with one comment. Only the Ready notice is once per head (`ReadyHead`).
- Eligibility: PR is read only when `ReadsPR(t)`: status **In Review**, no children, not design/design-review, labels not truncated, worker state **None or Idle**. A Working or Blocked worker costs no `gh` call. **So In Progress tickets, and In Review tickets with a working worker, are never read today.** An In Progress ticket with a PR is invisible to PR logic (the stall nudge covers idle In Progress workers and knows nothing about PRs).
- One action per ticket per tick (`watch` returns a single Action). `commentNudge` is tried first and takes the tick; stall/PR nudges fire a later tick. A Blocked worker is never nudged (planner skips; herdr also refuses typing into a blocked agent).
- No worker + In Review PR needs work: `prRelaunch` relaunches (Launch, counted by `RelaunchesAt` vs `NudgeLimit`); the nudge follows once the worker is Idle. Relaunches got a separate counter in commit 6311cb0 because a relaunch used to consume one of the two PR nudges.
- Problem detection is `pullrequest.Read` (internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go), the ONLY GitHub code: one `gh api graphql` call per eligible ticket per tick (30s timeout, `PRTimeout`), run in the repo dir, PR found by branch name (`headRefName`, OPEN, first 1). Query fetches `number url headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}} reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved} pageInfo{hasNextPage}}`. `PR{Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}`. Rollup state FAILURE or ERROR adds the single string "a failed check". PENDING/EXPECTED are not failures but block Ready. **The dispatcher learns only that the aggregate rollup failed: no check names, run IDs, URLs or logs.** A second failing check on the same head is indistinguishable. `Problem()` joins problems into one phrase ("a failed check, changes requested and a merge conflict"), so a failed check shares one nudge with other problems and one counter.

## Cache (`internal/cache/cache.go`)
`type Cache map[string]Entry` keyed by ticket identifier, persisted as indented JSON `cache.json`. Advisory ("deleting it loses little"): `Load` returns empty on missing OR corrupt file; unknown fields ignored; no version/migration; new `omitempty` fields are backward compatible.
`Entry` fields: LastStatus, LaunchFailures, Nudges, PRHead(omitempty), Relaunches, ResumePending, NotifyPending, ReadyHead, BlockedTicks, PendingComment, TicketID, CommentSeen, TeardownWarned.
- `NudgesAt(status, head)` / `RelaunchesAt` return 0 if `LastStatus != status || PRHead != head`, else the counter. A push (head moves) or status change resets.
- **`Entry` must stay comparable**: `dispatch.go:597` does `c[id] == (cache.Entry{})` to delete zero entries, so slice/map fields do not compile. A set of seen check-run IDs would need a string encoding, a bounded fixed set, or a change to that comparison.
- Pruning: only in `settle`'s tail for tickets missing from this tick's Linear read; entries for tickets still returned are never pruned, and per-ticket fields like `CommentSeen`/`ReadyHead` are kept only while a tree is leased.
- `settle` runs before actions: status change zeroes Nudges/Relaunches; if a PR was read it sets Nudges/Relaunches via the *At helpers and `PRHead=pr.Head`; if not read and status is not In Review it clears PRHead. Action effects after: successful non-comment Nudge does `e.Nudges++` and `ResumePending=false`; comment nudge only sets `CommentSeen`; Ready Notify sets `ReadyHead`; In Review Launch does `Relaunches++`; `escalate` zeroes Nudges and Relaunches. A refused herdr prompt is logged to stderr and counts for nothing; the next tick re-plans the same nudge (no failure flag; retry is by unchanged cache). Failed notifications by contrast reset counters (`NotifyPending`).

## Precedent: the comment nudge (decision 11, ENG-257, decision-log line 97)
"Dispatch is the event broker. Each tick it polls those sources, compares what it finds with its cache, and forwards what the receiver doesn't know yet... **Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves.**" The comment nudge is a separate rule with its own watermark `CommentSeen` and **counts toward neither the stall nor the PR limit**; it goes to working or idle workers (typing mid-turn delivers), skips a blocked worker and fires once unblocked (`PendingComments` holds the watermark back while a nudge is owed). Its text is fixed: `"%s has a new comment. Read the ticket's comments and act on them as your build skill says."`
Also: `ReadyHead` is a per-head "already told" marker; `Relaunches` is a separate counter; both follow the pattern "one counter or watermark per event kind".

## Worker side
- `skills/build/SKILL.md` line 10: "The dispatcher is the only clock, so run no /loop, cron or polling. A nudge from the dispatcher is your wake-up." Step 7: "Treat every review comment as a claim to check... A flaky check gets its own Backlog ticket and a re-run. A real failure gets fixed." Line 16: never go idle In Progress. Step 1: a ticket already In Review skips to step 7. Worker contract (blueprint 161-167): re-run a flake after filing a Backlog ticket, fix a real failure, escalate only for a decision or missing access; nudge text is treated as coming from the user.
- Nothing in the nudge names the failing check; the worker finds out itself (it has GitHub access via its own tools; "never poll" forbids timers, not looking after being told).
- Delivery: `herdr.Prompt` runs `herdr agent prompt <pane> <text>`; refuses a blocked agent. `dispatch tell` is the manual equivalent.
- Proposed but unapplied (decision-log 241-242): CI failures get one retry; second identical failure is real; "the nudge count resets on every push and a CodeRabbit fix loop never escalates" (a known cost of reset-on-push; future: count review rounds).
- `docs/guide.md` 65/76, `docs/config.md` 54 (nudge_limit semantics), `blueprint.md` 143-154, 230-238 (reconcile table: "A PR needs work when any check has failed..."), 244 (ready definition) describe current behavior; any change here must update them. Decision log entries are numbered; a new rule is a decision.

## Why the PR nudge is shaped this way (confidence tiers)
Documented: origin commit 9aae0e7 / PR #8 (ENG-232): "After two PR nudges with no push the ticket goes to Needs Human, and a push that moves the PR head resets the count." Nudges carry fixed text, no source tag. Inferred: head is the only progress signal in In Review, so "no push" means stuck; the dispatcher keeps one integer and recomputes the text from the live PR. Unknown: why 2, why `Problem()` joins into one phrase rather than one nudge per problem.
Constraints for any new event kind sharing the PR counter (inferred from the 6311cb0 precedent): it steals budget from PR-problem nudges; the escalation message ("without pushing") is wrong for events a push cannot fix; events that do not move the head never reset the count; Plan and settle must use the same helper or they disagree about the limit.

## Facts that bear directly on the decision
1. Today's data cannot support "once per failing check run": the query returns an aggregate state, no run IDs. New GitHub reads (check runs / `statusCheckRollup.contexts` with databaseId, name, conclusion, URL) are required; per-run identity is the cache key.
2. Today's read gate (In Review + idle/none worker) excludes In Progress and working workers. The Objective includes In Progress tickets, and typing into a working worker is already established for the comment nudge.
3. The existing "a failed check" PR problem keeps firing while the aggregate stays red; if both rules exist the worker could get a PR nudge and a check forward for the same failure. The relationship between them (suppress, replace, or tolerate) must be defined.
4. `Entry` comparability, `omitempty` compatibility, and the cache being advisory (a lost cache re-forwards failures already sent: bounded by what is still failing on the current head, but a duplicate message) shape what the cache can remember.
5. Cost: one `gh api graphql` per eligible ticket per tick today; widening the gate to In Progress/working workers raises calls per tick; no rate-limit handling exists beyond the 30s timeout.
6. Fixed-text convention: tests and the build skill depend on exact nudge wording; a check forward would need a new fixed template with variable parts (check name, URL).

# Candidate 1: a check forward with its own time watermark

## Problem

When a check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher should type one message into the ticket's worker per failed check run. Workers never poll (decision 11). Three things in today's code get in the way. `pullrequest.Read` only sees the aggregate rollup ("a failed check"), with no run identity. The PR read only happens for In Review tickets whose worker is idle or absent. And the PR nudge is a nag with a budget: `NudgeLimit` per (status, head), escalating "without pushing". The design has to fit `Entry` staying comparable (`dispatch.go:597`), the advisory cache, fixed nudge texts, one action per ticket per tick, and `settle` running before actions.

### Premise test

- **"The cache must remember which runs were forwarded (a set of run IDs)."** This premise is false. Every check run completes exactly once, and a re-run is a new run with a later `completedAt`. So one scalar watermark per ticket is enough to give "once per run": the newest forwarded completion time. Forward each failure whose `Done` is after it. This is the `CommentSeen` precedent with GitHub's clock in place of Linear's. Built from scratch, the dispatcher still needs memory, because a refused prompt or a blocked worker must leave the failure owed, and "failures since the last read" can't express that. But the memory is one `time.Time`, not a set. `Entry` stays comparable, needs no pruning and no string encoding.
- **"The PR read is gated to idle workers."** This is a cost optimisation from when only the idle nag consumed PRs. It is not a constraint. The comment nudge already types into working workers. The gate widens to idle or working workers on In Progress or In Review. Blocked workers stay unread, which is safe because their owed failures wait in the watermark.
- **"The PR nudge is the right place."** This is false. The PR nudge nags about *state*: it is bounded, counts toward a limit and escalates. A check failure is an *event*: it is delivered once, uses no budget and never escalates. Putting the event into the nag would need per-problem counters, would steal the budget (the 6311cb0 lesson), and would make "without pushing" wrong for a flake that is re-run without a push. So the answer is a separate rule. The PR nudge stays as it is.

## Usage (caller's view)

The tests bind to this. A fake `gh` serves `contexts` on the rollup, a fake herdr records the typed text, and the cache file shows the watermark.

```go
// pullrequest.Read now also returns the failed runs on the head.
pr, found, err := pullrequest.Read(ctx, gh, dir, branch, timeout)
// pr.Problems == ["a failed check"]            (unchanged, from the rollup)
// pr.Failed   == []pullrequest.FailedCheck{
```

- The PR nudge still says "a failed check" and can follow a forward on a stuck worker. This is deliberate and not a duplicate.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Extend the PR nudge** (per-check problems, shared `Nudges`). It stays shallow on identity, since the nudge still has no run IDs. It steals the nudge budget, makes "without pushing" wrong for flakes, and is limited by the idle-worker gate. It lost because the three event semantics conflict.
2. **A watermark** (`CheckSeen` as max run ID or max `completedAt`). Its state is one int64 and it needs no pruning, but completion order differs from ID order, so a slow run with a lower ID is missed. A second-resolution `completedAt` races on equal seconds. The told-set is exact and has no ordering assumption.
3. **A per-head flag** (`ChecksHead`, like `ReadyHead`). It is the structurally simplest, but it never reports a second failing check or a re-run failure on the same head, which the objective requires.
4. **Replace "a failed check" outright** with the forward. It has a shallower surface, but an ignored forward would leave an idle worker with a red PR and no escalation. It lost on the stuck-worker hole.

## Open questions and risks

- Does `statusCheckRollup.contexts` give a new node ID for each re-run and show only the latest run per check? This is assumed and should be verified against a real PR.
- Should a fix loop be bounded (for example, escalate after N forwards on one ticket), or is the known CodeRabbit-loop cost acceptable?
- Should neutral, cancelled and action_required runs ever count as failing?
- Is one batched message per tick acceptable for "one message per failing check run", or should each run get its own message across ticks?
- Is the told-set pruned wrongly if GitHub briefly omits a run from the rollup? The worst case is one duplicate.
- Docs to update: `docs/guide.md`, `blueprint.md` (the reconcile table at 230-238), and a new numbered decision-log entry.

## Next implementation step

Add `cache.RunSet` and `Entry.ChecksTold` with table tests for `With`, `Only`, `Minus` and zero-entry deletion, then widen the `pullrequest` query and write `FailedIDs` against the fake `gh`.

graders.name: last-message-asks-sketch
graders.evidence:
I stopped after the Phase B sketch, as you asked. I have not filed a ticket, saved a blueprint to Linear, written a `CONTEXT.md` or returned the tree. Nothing was compiled or run, and no repo files changed.

The files are in the working directory:
- `evidence.md`: grounding plus the three candidate rationales, joined with `cat`
- `artifact.md`: the synthesized design
- `note.md`: the synthesis note
- `scratch/grounding.md`: the Phase A trace

## Contract sketch

**It's its own rule, not an extension of the PR nudge.** The PR nudge is a stall detector. It sends at most `nudge_limit` messages per PR head, then escalates to Needs Human with "without pushing". A CI failure is an event. If the two shared a counter, the forward would use up the PR nudge budget, and "without pushing" would be wrong for a flake that gets re-run. A new `check nudge` step runs right after the comment nudge. It never touches `Nudges` or `Relaunches`.

**What the worker sees**, typed once per failing run:
```
PR https://github.com/o/r/pull/7 for ENG-9 has a failed check: unit (https://ci/1). Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says.
PR https://github.com/o/r/pull/7 for ENG-9 has 2 failed checks: unit (https://ci/1) and lint (https://ci/2). Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says.
```

**What the cache remembers:** one new field, `Entry.ChecksTold`, holding the GitHub node IDs of check runs that were told and are still failing.
- It is a sorted, comma-joined string, so `Entry` stays comparable and old cache files still load.
- It is pruned to the currently failing runs after every full read.
- The owed set is `live failing IDs − ChecksTold`.
- It is added to only after herdr accepts the message.

**What changes in the code:**
- `pullrequest.PR` gains `Failed []FailedCheck{ID, Name, URL}` and `FailedComplete`. The query widens to `statusCheckRollup.contexts`.
- The PR read widens to In Progress and In Review tickets whose worker is Idle or Working. Blocked workers are not read or typed to.
- `reconcile` gains `ReasonCheck` and `CheckNudge`.
- `Action` gains a `Checks` field, and the executor branches on it, not on `Reason`.
- `settle` keeps its `NudgesAt` and `PRHead` block for In Review only. Without that guard, reading In Progress PRs would reset the stall count on every push.
- The failing conclusions are FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, STARTUP_FAILURE and ACTION_REQUIRED, plus status FAILURE or ERROR. CANCELLED, SKIPPED and NEUTRAL are not forwarded.

**Failure behavior:**
- A refused prompt is retried next tick.
- A crash between send and save causes one duplicate, never a lost failure.
- A lost cache re-sends the runs that are still failing, once.
- A re-run that fails again has a new ID, so it is forwarded again.
- A push starts over.
- "A failed check" stays a PR problem. An idle worker that ignores the forward still gets the budgeted PR nudge and the Needs Human escalation.

**Considered and lost:**
- A completion-time watermark (candidates 1 and 2). It forwards once per completion time, not once per run, and it can miss a run on a tie or a late-visible run. A working worker has no fallback, because the PR nudge only reaches idle In Review workers.
- A per-head flag, which never reports a re-run failure on the same head.
- Replacing "a failed check", which leaves no escalation for an ignored failure.
- CI commenting on the Linear ticket.
- The worker running `gh pr checks --watch`, which breaks "workers never poll".

I also fixed one error in the base candidate. Its sketch cleared `ChecksTold` when a ticket changes status, which would re-forward a check that is still red when the ticket moves from In Progress to In Review. The artifact does not clear it.

## What you need to decide

1. **Approve or push back on the contract sketch.** If you push back on the shape, I re-ground and re-run the sketches.
2. **One message per run, or one message naming each run?** The Objective says "one message … once per failing check run". `Plan` returns one action per ticket per tick, so the design sends one message naming every run that fails in the same tick, and each run is named once. Sending a separate message per run would take one tick per run. I recommend batching.
3. **Is "a re-run gets a new check-run node ID" true?** The ID-based design depends on it. `gh` is unauthenticated here, so I couldn't check it against a real PR. One throwaway `gh api graphql` call on a real PR would settle it. If a provider updates a run in place, its re-fail would be missed.
4. **Which conclusions count as failing?** I excluded CANCELLED, SKIPPED and NEUTRAL and included ACTION_REQUIRED.
5. **Should In Progress tickets with no PR yet be skipped to save `gh` calls?** The design reads them every tick, about one extra call per ticket per 5-minute tick.
6. **Should a fix loop (push, new failure, forward, repeat) ever escalate?** As designed it never does, because each new run is a new event. This is the same cost the decision log already notes for reset-on-push.

I did not check the ticket text or PR bodies. `gh` is unauthenticated here and no Linear tools were used.

graders.evidence:
# Phase A grounding: forward a failing CI check to the owning worker

Approved Objective: when a check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide: extend the existing PR nudge or a new rule, and what the cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

Repo: Go module `dispatch` at the repo root. `git` fails on xcrun; use /opt/homebrew/bin/git. No `docs/adr/`. Design record: docs/design/{blueprint,decision-log}.md. Sources: four read-only investigators (PR flow, cache, PR/reconcile, git history). Linear, chat, docs, observability MCPs were NOT searched (none available). `gh` history not queried; merge commits and docs only. Spot-checked by me: reconcile.go:353 ReadsPR, dispatch.go:584-600 kept entry, pullrequest.go:53-64 query, decision-log.md decision 11.

## 1. What exists today (traced)

### Tick (dispatch.go `tick`, ~L209-516)
Takes `tick.lock` (flock, whole tick, so cache read-modify-write has no race), loads `<StateDir>/cache.json`, reads herdr, treehouse, Linear `ManagedTickets` (assigned, AI label, state.type started), then:
1. `input.PRs, input.PRReadFailed = readPRs(...)` (L332; defn L607-629). Loops tickets, skips unless `in.ReadsPR(t)`, calls `pullrequest.Read(ctx, gh, repoDir, t.Branch, PRTimeout)` once per eligible ticket, sequentially. Error -> stderr log, `failed[id]=true`, PR omitted; tick continues.
2. `reconcile.Plan(input)` (L333): PURE; returns `[]Action`.
3. `settle(...)` (L534) rolls the cache forward BEFORE actions run.
4. Action loop (L394-514). Nudge case L411-427: `herdr.Prompt(ctx, herdr, a.PaneID, a.Text)`; on error log and `continue` (refused prompt NOT counted); on success a `ReasonComment` nudge sets `e.CommentSeen = a.Ticket.LastComment`, any other nudge does `e.Nudges++; e.ResumePending=false`.
5. Deferred `c.Save` (skipped in dry run).

### Where nudges are decided (internal/reconcile/reconcile.go)
No rule interface or registry. `Input.watch(t) (Action, bool)` (L259) is a hard-coded sequence: skip truncated-label/`design` tickets; Needs Human -> Notify on entry; return unless status is In Progress or In Review and no children; `commentNudge` (L274, runs first, so one nudge per ticket per tick); then switch on worker state: Blocked -> Notify; Idle + In Review -> `inReviewIdle`; Idle + In Progress -> resume/stall nudge or Escalate at limit.
- `ReadsPR(t)` (L353-359): true only if status == InReview, labels not truncated, no children, no `design`/`design-review` label, worker state None or Idle. Working/Blocked workers cost no gh call. **In Progress tickets are never read.**
- `inReviewIdle` (L374-387): Ready && `prev.ReadyHead != pr.Head` -> Notify ReasonReady; not NeedsWork -> nothing; `prev.NudgesAt(status, head) >= NudgeLimit` (default 2) -> Escalate; else Nudge with `Reason = ReasonPR+": "+pr.Problem()`, `Text = fmt.Sprintf(PRNudge, pr.URL, ticket, pr.Problem())`.
- `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."` (L77). Wording is deliberately fixed (comment L72-73): tests assert exact strings (`prPrompt`, review_test.go L19) and decision-log L127 records "Fix it and push" was rejected because it told workers to skip step 7's evidence check.
- A gone worker (None) with a PR needing work is RELAUNCHED (`prRelaunch` L363; Plan L193-247), with its own `Relaunches` counter capped by NudgeLimit; relaunches skip `MaxInProgress`.
- `commentNudge` (L339-347) is the other forwarding rule: fires for Working OR Idle workers (not Blocked/None), In Progress and In Review, skips `design-review`; types `<ticket> has a new comment...` mid-turn. Counts toward neither stall nor PR limit and never escalates (decision-log L97-100).

### Typing into a worker
`herdr.Prompt(ctx, bin, pane, text)` (internal/herdr/herdr.go ~L102) runs `herdr agent prompt`; herdr refuses a blocked agent before any input. `tell.go` is the CLI `dispatch tell` and shares only `herdr.Prompt`. `worker.Find` maps ticket -> treehouse lease -> herdr workspace -> claude agent; `stateOf`: idle/done -> Idle, blocked -> Blocked, else Working.

### How GitHub is read (internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go)
`type PR struct{Number int; URL, Head string; Problems []string; Ready bool}`; `NeedsWork()`, `Problem()` join phrases ("a, b and c"). `Read` runs ONE `gh api graphql` (30s deadline, WaitDelay 1s): `pullRequests(headRefName:$branch, states:OPEN, first:1, orderBy UPDATED_AT DESC){ number url headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision commits(last:1){nodes{commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}}} reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved} pageInfo{hasNextPage}} }`. `>100` threads is an error, not a silent miss.
- Check handling L129-140: rollup `FAILURE`/`ERROR` -> Problem **"a failed check"**; any state != SUCCESS (PENDING, EXPECTED) -> `checksPassed=false` (blocks Ready, NOT a failure); nil rollup counts as passed. `Ready = !NeedsWork && checksPassed && mergeable==MERGEABLE`.
- The package never reads `contexts`, `checkRuns`, names, conclusions, `databaseId`, `completedAt`. No per-check identity exists anywhere. PR is found by Linear `branchName` == GitHub `headRefName`; no attachments.
- Cost: one GraphQL point per eligible ticket per tick; no ETag/cache.

### Cache (internal/cache/cache.go)
`type Cache map[string]Entry` keyed by ticket id; JSON at `<StateDir>/cache.json` (default `~/.local/state/dispatch`); atomic temp+rename save. Missing or corrupt file loads EMPTY (package doc: deleting the cache "loses little"). `Entry` fields: `LastStatus, LaunchFailures, Nudges, PRHead, Relaunches, ResumePending, NotifyPending, ReadyHead, BlockedTicks, PendingComment, TicketID, CommentSeen ("" never seen, "0" seen none), TeardownWarned` (most `omitempty`). `NudgesAt/RelaunchesAt(status, head)` return 0 when `LastStatus != status || PRHead != head` (a push or status change resets).
- Existing PR nudge memory = counter `Nudges` + `PRHead` + `LastStatus`. **It is not once-only**: it repeats each tick the worker is idle and the PR needs work, up to NudgeLimit, then Escalate to Needs Human. Reset only by head change/status change/escalate.
- Closest once-per-event precedents: **`CommentSeen`** (monotonic high-water mark; advanced only after a successful prompt; held back by `PendingComments()` while a nudge is owed) and **`ReadyHead`** (once per head; set only after the alert succeeds; failure leaves it unset so the next tick retries).
- `settle` (L534-600): zeroes Nudges/Relaunches/TeardownWarned on status change (L538); sets `e.Nudges = e.NudgesAt(...)`, `e.PRHead = pr.Head` when a PR was read (L565-568); an unread PR leaves PRHead (L563); a non-In-Review ticket with no PR clears it (L569). A ticket absent from the Linear read collapses to a `kept` Entry (L588): only `LaunchFailures, PendingComment, TicketID, TeardownWarned`, plus `CommentSeen` and `ReadyHead` while `leased[id]`. If it equals `cache.Entry{}` it is deleted. **`Entry` must stay comparable (`== cache.Entry{}` at dispatch.go L597): no slice/map fields.** Any new field is dropped on absence unless added to `kept`.
- `escalate()` (L641) resets Nudges/Relaunches. Docs to update with a new field: blueprint.md example JSON (~L272-287) and prose (~L289), docs/config.md only if config changes.

### Tests
Black-box `package dispatch_test`; `newHarness` (dispatch_test.go L464-521) writes bash fakes for herdr, gh, osascript, treehouse, launcher and a fake Linear httptest server; passes via `dispatch.Options`. No clock injection (only `PRTimeout`). Fake `gh` prints `pr-<branch>.json` (written by `h.pr(ticket, prState{head, checks string, decision, mergeable, unresolved...})`, review_test.go L25-56), logs each call to gh.log (`h.prReads()` counts), fails if `gh-fails` exists. `h.prompts()` returns `pane|text` lines; each `h.run("tick")` is one tick; state persists in cache.json in `h.state`. Tests assert call counts via `prReads()`, so reading In Progress tickets changes expectations. Existing CI tests: review_test.go L79-108 (FAILURE/ERROR -> "a failed check"), L217, L252, L278, L300, L322, L433, L500. No cache_test.go.

### Worker side
skills/build/SKILL.md: header says the dispatcher is the only clock and workers run no `/loop`, cron or polling; step 6 has a one-off `gh api ...protection` call; step 7 "Follow the PR to merge": a flaky check gets its own Backlog ticket and a re-run, a real failure gets fixed; nudges are treated as coming from the user. Nothing forbids a one-off `gh` call; polling is what is forbidden.

## 2. Recorded rationale (dispatch:why, source control + docs only)
- Decision 11 "Dispatch is the event broker" (ENG-257, 2026-10-09; decision-log L97): dispatcher polls GitHub/Linear each tick, compares with cache, forwards what the receiver doesn't know. "Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." Motivation (observed): ENG-255's worker missed a comment despite a build step telling it to read comments. The comment nudge is "one such rule, like the PR nudge."
- PR nudge origin: commit 9aae0e7 (PR #8, ENG-232); pilot: an In Review worker had no wake-up, a person nudged by hand twice (one for a CI run). "once per" language in the repo belongs to ReadyHead and CommentSeen; the PR nudge is a per-head budget of 2 (confirmed).
- Read gating (idle/gone only, one gh call, 30s deadline from 6311cb0 after a hung call held the tick lock). Count increments only after successful prompt (da32caa). Separate relaunch counter (6311cb0 fixed relaunch eating a PR nudge). Dispatcher text is fixed, untagged, comments on tickets only at Needs Human/dirty teardown (blueprint L63-66).
- Known gaps recorded: decision-log L241 proposes "CI failures get one retry; second identical failure is real; failure in code the diff never touched means rebase first" (build-skill change, not applied); L242 "count review rounds" since a CodeRabbit loop pushes every round and never escalates.

## 3. Constraints for a new CI-failure forward
Preserve: fixed untagged text from constants in reconcile.go; dispatcher-only detection; Plan stays pure and cache writes only after a successful `herdr.Prompt`; marker survives like CommentSeen/ReadyHead (kept while leased); Entry comparable; PENDING/EXPECTED are not failures; one GraphQL call per ticket per tick with the deadline; pointer to build step 7 (evidence check, flaky = own ticket + re-run); design/design-review/children/truncated-label exclusions; blocked workers skipped (typing lands in the question dialog) and forwarded once unblocked.
Change: In Progress tickets are never read (ReadsPR); the rollup gives no per-run identity or name; a failure while the worker is Working is invisible (comment nudge shows mid-turn typing is accepted); PR nudge is a repeating budget, not once; a re-run on the same head keeps `Head` so the head-keyed reset can't see it.
Avoid: worker polling/`gh pr checks` loops; reusing `Nudges` for CI forwards (would count toward escalation; comment nudge avoids this deliberately); counting refused prompts; reading PRs of Working workers without checking the call-count tests; silent pagination truncation; a slice/map in Entry.

## 4. Facts the design must decide (not yet settled)
1. Identity of a "failing check run": CheckRun `databaseId` (new per re-run) vs name+head; StatusContext has no id (use context name + `createdAt`/state).
2. A re-run on the same head that fails again: new run, forward again (per Objective wording "once per failing check run": yes).
3. Does a forward count against NudgeLimit/escalate, or never escalate (comment-nudge style)?
4. Marker shape that keeps Entry comparable: a single string high-water mark (e.g. latest forwarded `completedAt`+id) or a joined/sorted ID string; per head or global.
5. Extend `ReadsPR` to In Progress and to Working workers (call-count and cost impact; existing tests assert `prReads()`).
6. Message content: names failing check(s) and URL; must stay fixed-template, untagged, consistent with step 7.
7. Interaction with the existing "a failed check" PR problem (same event, two messages?) and with relaunch of a gone worker.

# Forward a failing CI check to the worker that owns the PR

## Problem

A check that fails on a ticket's PR should reach that ticket's worker exactly once per failing check run, typed by the dispatcher (decision 11: workers never poll). Three things in today's code stand in the way. First, detection reads only `statusCheckRollup.state`, so nothing has a per-run identity, and "once per run" can't be expressed. Second, `ReadsPR` reads PRs only for In Review tickets whose worker is None or Idle. A failure while the worker is Working, or on an In Progress ticket's draft PR, is never seen. Third, the only PR memory is `Nudges`+`PRHead`, which is a repeating per-head budget that escalates. It is not a once-only marker, and a re-run on the same head can't reset it.

Constraints carried over: Plan stays pure. Cache writes happen only after a successful `herdr.Prompt`. `cache.Entry` stays comparable. Each ticket gets one `gh api graphql` per tick with the 30s deadline. PENDING/EXPECTED are not failures. Message text is fixed, untagged and points at build step 7. Design, design-review, children and truncated-label tickets stay excluded. Blocked workers are never typed into.

**Premise challenged: "the existing PR nudge is the natural home, and PRs are read only for idle In Review workers."** If we built this from scratch with every signal now available, we would not fold CI forwarding into the PR nudge, and we would not keep the idle-only read gate. The two do different jobs. The PR nudge is *level-triggered*: "your PR is still in a bad state and you are idle", with a budget and escalation. Forwarding is *edge-triggered*: "this event happened", once per event, to a working or idle worker, and it never escalates. The comment nudge (decision 11's other rule, `commentNudge`) already has that edge-triggered shape, and it already types into Working workers mid-turn. The idle-only gate is a cost choice from 6311cb0, not a correctness constraint. A tick is every 5 minutes, and one GraphQL point per live ticket is negligible against 5000/hour. **Not a true constraint.** The rollup-only read is also not a constraint. It was all the PR nudge needed. So: **a new rule, `checkForward`, modelled on `commentNudge`**. The PR nudge stays unchanged as the idle-and-still-broken backstop that escalates.

# Forward a failing CI check to the owning worker (candidate 3)

## Premise check first

Baked-in premises: (a) the PR nudge is the natural home; (b) PRs are read only for idle In Review workers; (c) detection uses the aggregate rollup `statusCheckRollup.state`; (d) the cache dedupes with counter + head.

Would this mechanism exist if we built from scratch with every signal now available? No. The PR nudge is a repeating budget (`Nudges` < `NudgeLimit`, reset by head/status change) that answers "an idle In Review worker has a PR needing work". CI forwarding is an event forward ("a run you don't know about failed"). decision-log decision 11 already names that class: the comment nudge is "one such rule, like the PR nudge", and it deliberately uses its own marker (`CommentSeen`), fires for Working and Idle workers, and counts toward nothing. The rollup cannot support event semantics: it has no run identity, and a re-run on the same head leaves `Head` unchanged, so a counter+head key cannot see it. Premise (b) is a cost optimisation (6311cb0, a hung gh call held the tick lock), not a true constraint: reading is one deadline-bound GraphQL call and nothing forbids it for In Progress or Working workers. Premise (c) is not a constraint: the same query can return the per-run contexts. Premise (d) is true only for the PR nudge. Decision: **a new rule, modelled on `commentNudge`**, not an extension of `inReviewIdle`.

## Problem

A check fails on the PR of an In Progress or In Review ticket and today nobody tells the worker unless it is idle In Review and the aggregate is FAILURE/ERROR, and then only as a budgeted "a failed check" nudge. Constraints that hold: Plan is pure; cache writes follow a successful `herdr.Prompt`; `Entry` stays comparable (`== cache.Entry{}`, dispatch.go L597); text is a fixed untagged constant (tests assert exact strings); workers never poll; PENDING/EXPECTED are not failures; design/design-review/children/truncated-label tickets are excluded; a Blocked worker is not typed into.

## Usage (caller's view)

The user does nothing. Observable behaviour: a worker on ENG-300 (Working or Idle, In Progress or In Review) receives, within one tick of a run failing:

`CI check lint and unit failed on PR https://github.com/o/r/pull/9 for ENG-300. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push.`

and receives nothing more for those runs. A re-run that fails again is a new run and produces a new message. Tests:

```go
h.pr("ENG-300", prState{head: "a1", runs: []run{{id: 11, name: "lint", conclusion: "FAILURE"}}})
h.run("tick"); // h.prompts() has exactly one line containing "CI check lint failed"
h.run("tick"); // still one line; cache.json ENG-300.ci_forwarded == "c11"
h.pr("ENG-300", ...runs: {id: 12, name: "lint", conclusion: "FAILURE"})   // re-run, same head
h.run("tick"); // second line
```

## Shape

**Identity of a failing run.** `pullrequest.Check{Key, Name, URL}`. Key is `"c<databaseId>"` for a CheckRun (new id per re-run) and `"s<context>@<createdAt>"` for a StatusContext (no id exists; a re-posted status gets a new `createdAt`). Failing = CheckRun conclusion FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, STARTUP_FAILURE; StatusContext state FAILURE, ERROR. CANCELLED, SKIPPED, NEUTRAL, null (running) are not failures.

**GraphQL/PR change.** In the existing single query, expand `statusCheckRollup{state contexts(first:100){pageInfo{hasNextPage} nodes{__typename ... on CheckRun{databaseId name conclusion detailsUrl} ... on StatusContext{context state targetUrl createdAt}}}}`. `hasNextPage` is an error, exactly like the `>100` review threads rule (no silent miss). `PR` gains `FailedChecks []Check` (sorted by Key). The aggregate rollup, `Problems`, `Ready` and "a failed check" are unchanged. Wire types stay private in `pullrequest`.

**Cache.** One new field: `CIForwarded string` (`json:"ci_forwarded,omitempty"`), the `\n`-joined sorted Keys of failing runs already forwarded. A string, so `Entry` stays comparable. No head field: Keys are globally unique, so a new head's runs never collide, and each write sets the field to exactly the *currently failing* keys, which prunes it (bounded by the failing count, never grows across heads). Encoding is owned by one function, `PR.Unseen(seen) (fresh []Check, next string)`; cache, reconcile and dispatch treat the string as opaque (single owner, per the split-ownership flag).

- Written only in the action loop after `herdr.Prompt` returns nil: `e.CIForwarded = a.CIForwarded` (Plan computed `next`). A refused prompt `continue`s before the write, so the same `fresh` set is recomputed next tick.
- `settle` does not touch it, so status flips (In Progress -> In Review, same head) do not re-forward.
- Survives absence: added to the `kept` Entry while `leased[id]`, beside `CommentSeen`/`ReadyHead`; otherwise the entry collapses and a duplicate follows.
- Cache lost: empty string, so every still-failing run is forwarded once more, in one merged message. Acceptable and in the package's "deleting loses little" spirit: a still-failing run is by definition unfixed. No baseline sentinel (unlike `CommentSeen`'s "0") because the Objective wants pre-existing failures forwarded.

**Rule.** `Input.ciForward(t, pr, prev, w)` in `watch`, right after `commentNudge` and before the state switch: only for status In Progress/In Review and worker state Idle or Working (not Blocked, not None; a gone In Review worker is relaunched by the PR path, a gone In Progress worker is relaunched fresh). If `fresh` is empty, no action. Otherwise `Nudge{Reason: ReasonCI, Text: fmt.Sprintf(CINudge, names, pr.URL, ticket), CIForwarded: next}`. One message per tick covers all fresh runs; each run is forwarded in exactly one message. A pending comment nudge wins that tick; the CI marker is unwritten so it fires next tick (nothing lost).

`CINudge = "CI check %s failed on PR %s for %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."` Fixed, untagged, same step-7 pointer as `PRNudge` so the flaky-gets-own-ticket-and-rerun evidence check is kept; names are joined with the existing "a, b and c" helper.

**ReadsPR gating.** Becomes: status In Progress or In Review, labels not truncated, no children, no design/design-review, worker state Idle or Working; plus None for In Review (relaunch path, unchanged). Blocked is not read (forwarded once it unblocks, since the marker is unwritten). `settle` keeps writing `PRHead` only for In Review tickets, so an In Progress push does not reset the stall `Nudges` counter.

**Interaction with the existing problem.** CI forward does not touch `Nudges`/`Relaunches` and never escalates. The PR nudge keeps "a failed check" and stays the backstop: if the worker went idle again without fixing, the budgeted nudge then escalates to Needs Human at `NudgeLimit` as today. Relaunch of a gone In Review worker: the relaunch Action also carries `CIForwarded` (same `applyCI` helper as the nudge case) so the fresh worker is not told again next tick.

**Test entry.** Extend `prState` with `runs []run`; the fake gh JSON emits `contexts.nodes`. Observe via `h.prompts()` and `cache.json` in `h.state`. Cases: forward once over two ticks; re-run id forwarded again; refused prompt (blocked/refusing fake herdr) leaves `ci_forwarded` absent and retries; Blocked then unblocked forwards once; delete cache.json re-forwards once; ticket dropped from Linear while leased keeps the field; PENDING/CANCELLED/SKIPPED never forward; `hasNextPage` errors; In Progress Working worker is read (update existing `prReads()` expectations for Working/In Progress tickets).

**Correctness argument.** (1) No duplicate: ticks are serialised by `tick.lock`; Plan emits a Key only if absent from `prev.CIForwarded`; the field is written after the successful prompt in the same tick and saved by the deferred `Save`; Keys are unique per run, so no other path (head change, status change, relaunch, escalate, re-read) re-creates an unseen Key. Relaunch writes the same field. Dry run neither prompts nor writes. (2) No loss on refusal: the write is after success, so `fresh` is recomputed identically. (3) Writes set the field to the current failing set, which is a superset of what was just delivered, so a run that fails later (different Key) is always fresh, regardless of completion order (no high-water mark, which would lose a long job finishing after a short one). Residual: a crash between a successful `Prompt` and `Save` can duplicate (at-least-once), same as every existing rule.

## Synthesis decision

filled by orchestrator

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept two messages for one failure (CI forward, then the PR nudge if the worker idles unfixed) in exchange for keeping the escalation backstop and the relaunch path untouched.
- We accept reading In Progress/Working tickets (more gh calls; most return no PR) in exchange for forwarding a failure mid-turn, as comment nudge already does.
- We accept re-forwarding after cache loss in exchange for a single string field and no baseline sentinel.
- We accept that a flaky re-run loop forwards forever (each fail is a new run) and never escalates in exchange for matching "once per failing check run".

## Alternatives considered

- Extend `inReviewIdle` with per-run memory: rejected; it is gated to idle In Review and counts against escalation, so mid-turn and In Progress failures stay invisible. Exposes counter semantics to a non-counter event.
- High-water mark (`completedAt`/max id) like `CommentSeen`: smaller, but loses a slower job that finishes after a faster one already advanced the mark.
- Per-head `CIHead`+set: redundant, since Keys are unique and pruning by presence bounds the set.
- Worker-side `gh pr checks` polling: forbidden by decision 11.
- Webhook/event push: no inbound surface; the dispatcher is the only clock.

## Open questions and risks

- Should a run re-forwarded N times on the same head (flaky loop) escalate? decision-log L241 proposes "second identical failure is real"; do we add a cap now or leave it?
- Is >100 contexts on one commit realistic in target repos, given it fails the read for that ticket?
- Does `herdr` accept mid-turn typing for all agent states as the comment nudge assumes?
- Sequential 30s-deadline reads now cover more tickets under `tick.lock`; do we need a per-tick budget?
- Does the relaunch Action path have one place to apply the marker, or two?

## Next implementation step

Add `Check`, `FailedChecks` and `PR.Unseen` to `internal/pullrequest` with the expanded query and a table test of the key/prune encoding.

graders.name: last-message-asks-sketch
graders.evidence:
The CI-failure forward should be its own rule, modelled on the comment nudge, and not an extension of the existing pull request nudge. I stopped after the Phase A grounding and the Phase B sketch, as you asked. Nothing was compiled and no repo file was edited. All three candidates (opus, fable, sonnet) reached this shape on their own, and the cross-judge picked candidate 1 as the base.

The files are `scratch/grounding.md`, `evidence.md`, `artifact.md` and `note.md`.

## Contract sketch

**Why a new rule.** The PR nudge repeats up to a limit while the worker is idle, then escalates. A CI failure is a one-time event.
- Today's code reads only idle In Review workers.
- It sees only the combined check state ("a failed check"), with no way to tell one run from another.
- The comment nudge already fits an event like this: it fires for working and idle workers and never escalates. The PR nudge stays unchanged as the backstop.

**What the worker sees.** One message per tick, naming every newly failed run:
`CI failed on PR <url> for ENG-1: test (<run url>) and lint (<run url>). Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push.`

**Which runs count.**
- **Run identity:** each failing run gets an opaque key. A check run uses its GitHub id, and a re-run gets a new id, so a re-run that fails again is forwarded again. A commit status uses a hash of its context name and creation time.
- **Counts as failed:** a failure, timeout or startup failure on a check run, and a failure or error on a commit status.
- **Does not count:** pending, cancelled, skipped, neutral and action-required runs.
- **Query:** the existing GitHub query also returns the individual checks, up to 100. More than 100 is an error, the same as for review threads.

**What the cache remembers.**
- **The field:** one new field, `checks_forwarded`, holding the sorted keys of the failing runs already typed to the worker. Plan sends only the failing runs not in that set.
- **When it is written:** only after the prompt lands, and the new value is the keys failing at that moment. A refused prompt, a blocked worker, a failed GitHub read, a tick taken by a comment nudge, and a dry run all leave it alone, so the failure is sent on a later tick.
- **Absent tickets:** it is kept for an absent ticket only while its tree is leased, like the comment marker.
- **Cache loss:** if the cache is lost, runs still failing are forwarded once more.
- **Limits:** forwards never count toward the nudge limit and never escalate.

**Which pull requests get read.** In Progress or In Review tickets whose worker is idle or working, plus a gone In Review worker for relaunch. Blocked workers are not read.

**A bug I verified.** `settle` in `dispatch.go` (around line 565) updates the stall counter and PR head for any ticket whose PR was read. Once In Progress pull requests are read, every push would reset the stall count. The design limits that block to In Review, and adds the same check to `prRelaunch`. Only candidate 1 had this.

**What I took from the others:**
- Candidate 3: store "keys failing now", which makes the cache type simpler.
- Candidate 2: its test list, and letting the dry-run line carry check names.

**What I rejected:**
- Candidate 2's head-scoped marker.
- Counting cancelled and action-required runs as failures.
- Candidate 3's marking runs as forwarded on relaunch, which records a forward nobody received.

**Tests.** One existing test inverts on purpose: `TestTickDoesNotReadThePRWhileTheInReviewWorkerIsBusy`. A busy worker's pull request is now read, but no PR nudge is sent.

## What you must decide next

Approve or reject the contract sketch above. If you reject it, I re-ground and re-run Phase B. Four questions are still open, with my default for each:
1. Should repeated CI failures ever escalate to Needs Human? A push, fail, push, fail loop is uncapped under this design. My default is no cap for now.
2. Should cancelled runs be forwarded? My default is no.
3. Is it acceptable that every ticket with a still-failing run gets one forward on the first tick after rollout? My default is yes.
4. Is the step-7 pointer right for an In Progress worker that hasn't reached step 7 yet? That needs a call from you or the build skill owner.

One thing is unverified: the GitHub query field names (`contexts`, `databaseId`, and so on) come from the documented schema, not a live call, because the sandbox has no network. Confirm them before building.

# Grounding: forwarding a failing CI check to the worker that owns the PR

Repo: dispatch (Go). Phase A over three subsystems (PR nudge, tick/cache/settle, worker delivery incl. comment nudge) plus the history behind them. All paths relative to repo root. Line numbers are from the explorers' reads; verify before pinning.

## Approved Objective
When a check fails on the pull request of an In Progress or In Review ticket, the dispatcher types one message into that ticket's worker, once per failing check run, so the worker fixes it without the user relaying anything. Workers never poll GitHub. Decide whether this extends the existing pull request nudge or becomes its own rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## 1. How the system runs
`tick` (dispatch.go:209-516): take flock `StateDir/tick.lock` (internal/lock) -> load cache (`StateDir/cache.json`) -> register a deferred atomic Save (skipped on --dry-run) -> read herdr, treehouse, Linear (`ManagedTickets`) -> `readPRs` (dispatch.go:603) -> `reconcile.Plan(input)` (pure; reads cache, never writes) -> retry `PendingComment` -> `settle` (dispatch.go:534-601) -> execute Actions (switch at 394-514) -> deferred Save.
`reconcile` is pure and shared with dry-run. `dispatch.go` is the only executor. Tests are surface tests at repo root (package dispatch_test) with a fake `gh` returning JSON (harness `h.pr`, `prState`, review_test.go:44-61, `prPrompt` review_test.go:19) and a fake herdr.

## 2. Existing PR nudge (what a failing check does today)
Data: `pullrequest.Read` (internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go:68-155) makes ONE `gh api graphql` call per ticket per tick (30s bound). Query: `number url headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}} reviewThreads(first:100){isResolved}`. Kept: `PR{Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}`. The ONLY check data is the rollup `state` of the last commit. FAILURE or ERROR appends the fixed phrase "a failed check" (133-136). PENDING/EXPECTED are neither problem nor ready. No check names, run ids, contexts, checkSuites anywhere in Go code. `Ready` = no problems, rollup SUCCESS/absent, MERGEABLE.
Who is read: `ReadsPR` (reconcile.go:353-359): status == In Review only, worker state None or Idle only (a Working/Blocked worker costs no gh call, TestTickDoesNotReadThePRWhileTheInReviewWorkerIsBusy), no children, no truncated labels, not `design`/`design-review`. In Progress tickets are never PR-read. A read error sets `PRReadFailed` and skips the ticket (distinct from "no PR").
Rule: `watch` (reconcile.go:259-304) runs `commentNudge` first, then by worker state: Blocked -> notify only; Idle + In Review -> `inReviewIdle` (374-387); Working -> nothing for PRs.
`inReviewIdle`: if pr.Ready and prev.ReadyHead != pr.Head -> Notify the human (once per head). If PR absent or !NeedsWork -> nothing. Else n := prev.NudgesAt(status, pr.Head); n >= NudgeLimit -> Escalate (Needs Human + one comment, "stayed idle through N nudges about URL without pushing"); else Nudge with `PRNudge`.
Text (reconcile.go:72-81, fixed on purpose: "the build-worker skill and the tests rely on" exact wording; worker treats nudges as from the user): `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."`, Reason `"PR needs work: <problem>"`. "Fix it and push" was replaced because it made workers skip step 7's claim-checking (decision-log.md ~127).
Repeat semantics: NOT once-per-failure. While the worker is idle and any problem persists, a nudge goes out EVERY tick up to NudgeLimit (default 2, internal/config/config.go:59) per (status, head), then Escalate. Review comments, threads, conflicts and failing checks share one folded text and one `Nudges` budget. A new head (push) or status change zeroes the count. A rerun of a check on the SAME sha is invisible (same head, same rollup state). A busy worker is never told; a failure appearing while it works is seen only when it goes idle.
No worker (state None) on In Review with NeedsWork: `prRelaunch` (363-369) -> Launch with Reason "PR needs work: ..." bypassing MaxInProgress; bounded by `Relaunches` (separate counter so a relaunch does not eat a PR nudge, commit 6311cb0); at limit Escalate.
Executor Nudge case (dispatch.go:411-427): `herdr.Prompt`; on failure log + `continue`, nothing counted (retried next tick; TestTickDoesNotCountANudgeHerdrRefused). On success: ReasonComment -> `CommentSeen = a.Ticket.LastComment`, nothing else; any other nudge -> `Nudges++`, `ResumePending=false`. The executor special-cases only `ReasonComment`; a new Reason would fall into `Nudges++` unless added.

## 3. Existing exactly-once precedent: the comment nudge
Identity is a monotonic time, `Ticket.LastComment` (createdAt of newest comment, filled only by `ManagedTickets`, linear.go:38-41,144,219), compared as a string against `Entry.CommentSeen`. `CommentDue` (reconcile.go:309): CommentSeen != "" && LastComment > CommentSeen. Empty CommentSeen = first sighting: record without nudging (so a deleted cache or new ticket does not replay old comments). `commentNudge` (339-347) goes to Working OR Idle workers, In Progress or In Review, never Blocked/None, skips design-review, defers to resume nudge. It is NOT counted toward stall or PR limits and never escalates (commit acf73c8; decision 11).
Cursor discipline: `settle` advances CommentSeen to LastComment ("0" if none) unless `PendingComments` (318-332) holds it back. Held when a nudge is owed, worker Blocked, or worker None in unread repo. The nudge rule and the hold rule call the same function, so they cannot disagree. Success in the executor sets the cursor; refusal leaves it, so retry next tick. For tickets leaving the managed read the cursor survives only while a tree is leased (dispatch.go:~591).
Comment nudge costs no extra call (rides the ticket query; TestTickCommentNudgeMakesNoExtraLinearCall). Tests: comment_test.go (once per comment for busy and idle workers, retries after herdr refusal, not counted, never escalates).

## 4. Cache and settle
`cache.Entry` (internal/cache/cache.go): LastStatus, LaunchFailures, Nudges, PRHead, Relaunches, ResumePending, NotifyPending, ReadyHead, BlockedTicks, PendingComment, TicketID, CommentSeen, TeardownWarned. JSON map keyed by ticket identifier. No schema version; unknown fields ignored, missing read as zero, so adding a field is safe. Atomic save (temp + rename) only in the tick's defer. Missing OR corrupt file -> empty cache silently (89-92). Package doc: deleting the cache "loses little" (counters reset, a ready PR re-notifies, first tick re-records CommentSeen). Design constraint to preserve.
`NudgesAt/RelaunchesAt` (61-74) return 0 if LastStatus != status or PRHead != head; shared by Plan and settle so they cannot disagree.
`settle` per ticket: status change zeroes Nudges, Relaunches, TeardownWarned; sets PRHead/Nudges/Relaunches from the read PR; clears PRHead when not In Review; a busy/failed read in In Review keeps the stale PRHead so a later push is still seen. Pruning (581-600): entries for tickets not in this tick's Linear read are rebuilt field by field keeping only LaunchFailures, PendingComment, TicketID, TeardownWarned (if not held), and CommentSeen/ReadyHead if leased. A new field is DROPPED on pruning unless added to that kept list. No TTL or size cap.
Crash between send and save: sends are at-least-once (prompt first, record after; no write-ahead). A kill after herdr.Prompt and before the deferred Save re-sends next tick. True for comments, PR nudges, ready alerts. No test covers it.
Undo idiom: alert failure hand-resets BlockedTicks/NotifyPending (dispatch.go:466-473); otherwise `continue` leaves state unadvanced.
Other once-flags and their resets: ReadyHead (once per head, written only after alert succeeds, survives read gaps, 903637b), TeardownWarned (dropped when ticket stops being a finished leased ticket).

## 5. Worker delivery
`herdr.Prompt` (internal/herdr/herdr.go:99-108): `<bin> agent prompt <pane> <text>`; herdr itself refuses a Blocked agent before sending input. `worker.Find/onTree` (internal/worker/worker.go): lease holder = ticket id -> herdr workspace whose CheckoutPath equals the tree -> agent Kind=="claude". States None/Working/Idle/Blocked; herdr idle|done -> Idle, blocked -> Blocked, everything else (incl. unknown) -> Working. The state is a snapshot from the start of the tick, so a worker can turn Blocked before the prompt (refusal path handles it). Typing into a Working worker is allowed (comment nudge does it).
Skip rules in `watch`: LabelsTruncated or `design` label -> nothing; only In Progress/In Review nudged; HasChildren -> skipped; `design-review` skipped by commentNudge, stall nudge, ReadsPR, PendingComments.
Worker skill (skills/build/SKILL.md): line 10 "The dispatcher is the only clock, so run no /loop, cron or polling"; "a nudge from the dispatcher is your wake-up, and its text comes from the user". Step 7 (line 29): treat each review comment as a claim to verify; "A flaky check gets its own Backlog ticket and a re-run. A real failure gets fixed." Step 7 does not mention gh; nudges say what happened and the worker investigates.
`internal/commenteval` is an unrelated eval harness for needs-human comments, not nudge code.

## 6. Why (history)
Sources: git history, docs/design/blueprint.md, decision-log.md, code comments. `gh` offline, Linear not queried: PR/ticket discussion text is a COVERAGE GAP.
- Decision 11 "Dispatch is the event broker" (ENG-257, acf73c8, decision-log ~97): dispatch polls GitHub and Linear each tick, compares to its cache, forwards what the receiver does not know yet. "Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." Trigger: a worker missed a comment posted minutes before its PR. (decision-log ~117: workers run no /loop/cron/babysit; the dispatcher is the only clock; a nudge is a worker's only wake-up.)
- PR nudge origin: PR #4 (an In Review worker stopped and waited), ENG-232 (9aae0e7, PR #8): "After two PR nudges with no push the ticket goes to Needs Human, and a push that moves the PR head resets the count." The counter measures an unresponsive idle worker, not distinct failures; a repeat for the same unfixed problem is the intended retry, Needs Human the backstop. Inferred, not written.
- Rollup-only read: blueprint.md ~300 says one GraphQL call reads head, checks, review decision, mergeability and threads (gh pr view lacks threads). No recorded reason against per-check data; unknown whether contexts/checkSuites was considered. Cost bound: gh calls only for idle/gone In Review workers.
- Comments use a timestamp cursor because they are an append-only event stream (deliver once); PR problems are a persisting condition (count of unresponsiveness). No text states this contrast.
- decision-log ~242 (proposed, unapplied): "the nudge count resets on every push and a CodeRabbit fix loop never escalates"; suggests counting review rounds. Any change to the nudge counter may collide.
- Convention: imperative commit subjects with no ticket id; behavior changes update blueprint.md (nudges, cache schema, reconcile table, scale), decision-log.md ("applied, ENG-nnn"), guide.md (~76), config.md (~54 nudge_limit) in the same change; surface tests in root *_test.go; Go for all new scripts (CLAUDE.md). No docs/adr/ directory exists; decisions live in docs/design/decision-log.md.

## 7. Facts that constrain the design
1. "Once per failing check run" cannot be derived from today's data. Needs a new read (statusCheckRollup contexts: CheckRun name/databaseId/conclusion/completedAt/url, plus StatusContext for legacy statuses; mind 100-node page limit, and the repo's rule that a missed second page is an error) and a cache field of forwarded run identities.
2. Today's read happens only for In Review + Idle/None workers. The Objective also covers In Progress tickets and (by "types into the worker") Working workers. Either widen ReadsPR (costs gh calls per working ticket per tick) or accept delivery only at idle. In Progress tickets with an open PR are not PR-read at all today.
3. A rerun on the same sha yields a new check run id on the same head; head-keyed counters cannot see it. Per-run identity must not be reset by a head change in a way that re-forwards runs of an old head, and must not accumulate forever (pruning rules, bounded size).
4. Both existing nudges can fire for one failure: the PR nudge would re-nudge "a failed check" each tick up to NudgeLimit. A new rule must not double-send for the same failure (two ways to do one task) nor silently multiply the NudgeLimit budget.
5. Exactly-once is at-least-once-in-fact (crash between send and save). Comment cursor has the same property; acceptable precedent, must be stated.
6. Executor `Nudges++` branch special-cases ReasonComment only; the sole place a new reason must be handled. Pruning kept-list is the second place a new cache field must be registered. Text fixed and tested; any new text must be a constant in reconcile.go.
7. Escalation: comment nudges never escalate; PR nudges escalate at NudgeLimit. Whether a forwarded failure that the worker never fixes escalates is undecided by precedent.

# Grounding: forwarding a failing CI check to the worker that owns the PR

Repo: dispatch (Go). Phase A over three subsystems (PR nudge, tick/cache/settle, worker delivery incl. comment nudge) plus the history behind them. All paths relative to repo root. Line numbers are from the explorers' reads; verify before pinning.

Workers never poll GitHub. Decide whether this extends the existing pull request nudge or becomes its own rule, and what the dispatcher's cache must remember so a failure is forwarded once.

## 1. How the system runs
`tick` (dispatch.go:209-516): take flock `StateDir/tick.lock` (internal/lock) -> load cache (`StateDir/cache.json`) -> register a deferred atomic Save (skipped on --dry-run) -> read herdr, treehouse, Linear (`ManagedTickets`) -> `readPRs` (dispatch.go:603) -> `reconcile.Plan(input)` (pure; reads cache, never writes) -> retry `PendingComment` -> `settle` (dispatch.go:534-601) -> execute Actions (switch at 394-514) -> deferred Save.
`reconcile` is pure and shared with dry-run. `dispatch.go` is the only executor. Tests are surface tests at repo root (package dispatch_test) with a fake `gh` returning JSON (harness `h.pr`, `prState`, review_test.go:44-61, `prPrompt` review_test.go:19) and a fake herdr.

## 2. Existing PR nudge (what a failing check does today)
Data: `pullrequest.Read` (internal/pullrequest/pullrequest.go:68-155) makes ONE `gh api graphql` call per ticket per tick (30s bound). Query: `number url headRefOid mergeable reviewDecision commits(last:1){commit{statusCheckRollup{state}}} reviewThreads(first:100){isResolved}`. Kept: `PR{Number, URL, Head, Problems []string, Ready bool}`. The ONLY check data is the rollup `state` of the last commit. FAILURE or ERROR appends the fixed phrase "a failed check" (133-136). PENDING/EXPECTED are neither problem nor ready. No check names, run ids, contexts, checkSuites anywhere in Go code. `Ready` = no problems, rollup SUCCESS/absent, MERGEABLE.
Who is read: `ReadsPR` (reconcile.go:353-359): status == In Review only, worker state None or Idle only (a Working/Blocked worker costs no gh call, TestTickDoesNotReadThePRWhileTheInReviewWorkerIsBusy), no children, no truncated labels, not `design`/`design-review`. In Progress tickets are never PR-read. A read error sets `PRReadFailed` and skips the ticket (distinct from "no PR").
Rule: `watch` (reconcile.go:259-304) runs `commentNudge` first, then by worker state: Blocked -> notify only; Idle + In Review -> `inReviewIdle` (374-387); Working -> nothing for PRs.
`inReviewIdle`: if pr.Ready and prev.ReadyHead != pr.Head -> Notify the human (once per head). If PR absent or !NeedsWork -> nothing. Else n := prev.NudgesAt(status, pr.Head); n >= NudgeLimit -> Escalate (Needs Human + one comment, "stayed idle through N nudges about URL without pushing"); else Nudge with `PRNudge`.
Text (reconcile.go:72-81, fixed on purpose: "the build-worker skill and the tests rely on" exact wording; worker treats nudges as from the user): `PRNudge = "PR %s for %s has %s. Handle it as your build skill's step 7 says, and push."`, Reason `"PR needs work: <problem>"`. "Fix it and push" was replaced because it made workers skip step 7's claim-checking (decision-log.md ~127).
Repeat semantics: NOT once-per-failure. While the worker is idle and any problem persists, a nudge goes out EVERY tick up to NudgeLimit (default 2, internal/config/config.go:59) per (status, head), then Escalate. Review comments, threads, conflicts and failing checks share one folded text and one `Nudges` budget. A new head (push) or status change zeroes the count. A rerun of a check on the SAME sha is invisible (same head, same rollup state). A busy worker is never told; a failure appearing while it works is seen only when it goes idle.
No worker (state None) on In Review with NeedsWork: `prRelaunch` (363-369) -> Launch with Reason "PR needs work: ..." bypassing MaxInProgress; bounded by `Relaunches` (separate counter so a relaunch does not eat a PR nudge, commit 6311cb0); at limit Escalate.
Executor Nudge case (dispatch.go:411-427): `herdr.Prompt`; on failure log + `continue`, nothing counted (retried next tick; TestTickDoesNotCountANudgeHerdrRefused). On success: ReasonComment -> `CommentSeen = a.Ticket.LastComment`, nothing else; any other nudge -> `Nudges++`, `ResumePending=false`. The executor special-cases only `ReasonComment`; a new Reason would fall into `Nudges++` unless added.

## 3. Existing exactly-once precedent: the comment nudge
Identity is a monotonic time, `Ticket.LastComment` (createdAt of newest comment, filled only by `ManagedTickets`, linear.go:38-41,144,219), compared as a string against `Entry.CommentSeen`. `CommentDue` (reconcile.go:309): CommentSeen != "" && LastComment > CommentSeen. Empty CommentSeen = first sighting: record without nudging (so a deleted cache or new ticket does not replay old comments). `commentNudge` (339-347) goes to Working OR Idle workers, In Progress or In Review, never Blocked/None, skips design-review, defers to resume nudge. It is NOT counted toward stall or PR limits and never escalates (commit acf73c8; decision 11).
Cursor discipline: `settle` advances CommentSeen to LastComment ("0" if none) unless `PendingComments` (318-332) holds it back. Held when a nudge is owed, worker Blocked, or worker None in unread repo. The nudge rule and the hold rule call the same function, so they cannot disagree. Success in the executor sets the cursor; refusal leaves it, so retry next tick. For tickets leaving the managed read the cursor survives only while a tree is leased (dispatch.go:~591).
Comment nudge costs no extra call (rides the ticket query; TestTickCommentNudgeMakesNoExtraLinearCall). Tests: comment_test.go (once per comment for busy and idle workers, retries after herdr refusal, not counted, never escalates).

## 4. Cache and settle
`cache.Entry` (internal/cache/cache.go): LastStatus, LaunchFailures, Nudges, PRHead, Relaunches, ResumePending, NotifyPending, ReadyHead, BlockedTicks, PendingComment, TicketID, CommentSeen, TeardownWarned. JSON map keyed by ticket identifier. No schema version; unknown fields ignored, missing read as zero, so adding a field is safe. Atomic save (temp + rename) only in the tick's defer. Missing OR corrupt file -> empty cache silently (89-92). Package doc: deleting the cache "loses little" (counters reset, a ready PR re-notifies, first tick re-records CommentSeen). Design constraint to preserve.
`NudgesAt/RelaunchesAt` (61-74) return 0 if LastStatus != status or PRHead != head; shared by Plan and settle so they cannot disagree.
`settle` per ticket: status change zeroes Nudges, Relaunches, TeardownWarned; sets PRHead/Nudges/Relaunches from the read PR; clears PRHead when not In Review; a busy/failed read in In Review keeps the stale PRHead so a later push is still seen. Pruning (581-600): entries for tickets not in this tick's Linear read are rebuilt field by field keeping only LaunchFailures, PendingComment, TicketID, TeardownWarned (if not held), and CommentSeen/ReadyHead if leased. A new field is DROPPED on pruning unless added to that kept list. No TTL or size cap.
Crash between send and save: sends are at-least-once (prompt first, record after; no write-ahead). A kill after herdr.Prompt and before the deferred Save re-sends next tick. True for comments, PR nudges, ready alerts. No test covers it.
Undo idiom: alert failure hand-resets BlockedTicks/NotifyPending (dispatch.go:466-473); otherwise `continue` leaves state unadvanced.
Other once-flags and their resets: ReadyHead (once per head, written only after alert succeeds, survives read gaps, 903637b), TeardownWarned (dropped when ticket stops being a finished leased ticket).

## 5. Worker delivery
`herdr.Prompt` (internal/herdr/herdr.go:99-108): `<bin> agent prompt <pane> <text>`; herdr itself refuses a Blocked agent before sending input. `worker.Find/onTree` (internal/worker/worker.go): lease holder = ticket id -> herdr workspace whose CheckoutPath equals the tree -> agent Kind=="claude". States None/Working/Idle/Blocked; herdr idle|done -> Idle, blocked -> Blocked, everything else (incl. unknown) -> Working. The state is a snapshot from the start of the tick, so a worker can turn Blocked before the prompt (refusal path handles it). Typing into a Working worker is allowed (comment nudge does it).
Skip rules in `watch`: LabelsTruncated or `design` label -> nothing; only In Progress/In Review nudged; HasChildren -> skipped; `design-review` skipped by commentNudge, stall nudge, ReadsPR, PendingComments.
Worker skill (skills/build/SKILL.md): line 10 "The dispatcher is the only clock, so run no /loop, cron or polling"; "a nudge from the dispatcher is your wake-up, and its text comes from the user". Step 7 (line 29): treat each review comment as a claim to verify; "A flaky check gets its own Backlog ticket and a re-run. A real failure gets fixed." Step 7 does not mention gh; nudges say what happened and the worker investigates.
`internal/commenteval` is an unrelated eval harness for needs-human comments, not nudge code.

## 6. Why (history)
Sources: git history, docs/design/blueprint.md, decision-log.md, code comments. `gh` offline, Linear not queried: PR/ticket discussion text is a COVERAGE GAP.
- Decision 11 "Dispatch is the event broker" (ENG-257, acf73c8, decision-log ~97): dispatch polls GitHub and Linear each tick, compares to its cache, forwards what the receiver does not know yet. "Workers never poll. A new kind of event is a new forwarding rule in the dispatcher, never an instruction for workers to check something themselves." Trigger: a worker missed a comment posted minutes before its PR. (decision-log ~117: workers run no /loop/cron/babysit; the dispatcher is the only clock; a nudge is a worker's only wake-up.)
- PR nudge origin: PR #4 (an In Review worker stopped and waited), ENG-232 (9aae0e7, PR #8): "After two PR nudges with no push the ticket goes to Needs Human, and a push that moves the PR head resets the count." The counter measures an unresponsive idle worker, not distinct failures; a repeat for the same unfixed problem is the intended retry, Needs Human the backstop. Inferred, not written.
- Rollup-only read: blueprint.md ~300 says one GraphQL call reads head, checks, review decision, mergeability and threads (gh pr view lacks threads). No recorded reason against per-check data; unknown whether contexts/checkSuites was considered. Cost bound: gh calls only for idle/gone In Review workers.
- Comments use a timestamp cursor because they are an append-only event stream (deliver once); PR problems are a persisting condition (count of unresponsiveness). No text states this contrast.
- decision-log ~242 (proposed, unapplied): "the nudge count resets on every push and a CodeRabbit fix loop never escalates"; suggests counting review rounds. Any change to the nudge counter may collide.
- Convention: imperative commit subjects with no ticket id; behavior changes update blueprint.md (nudges, cache schema, reconcile table, scale), decision-log.md ("applied, ENG-nnn"), guide.md (~76), config.md (~54 nudge_limit) in the same change; surface tests in root *_test.go; Go for all new scripts (CLAUDE.md). No docs/adr/ directory exists; decisions live in docs/design/decision-log.md.

## 7. Facts that constrain the design
1. "Once per failing check run" cannot be derived from today's data. Needs a new read (statusCheckRollup contexts: CheckRun name/databaseId/conclusion/completedAt/url, plus StatusContext for legacy statuses; mind 100-node page limit, and the repo's rule that a missed second page is an error) and a cache field of forwarded run identities.
2. Today's read happens only for In Review + Idle/None workers. The Objective also covers In Progress tickets and (by "types into the worker") Working workers. Either widen ReadsPR (costs gh calls per working ticket per tick) or accept delivery only at idle. In Progress tickets with an open PR are not PR-read at all today.
3. A rerun on the same sha yields a new check run id on the same head; head-keyed counters cannot see it. Per-run identity must not be reset by a head change in a way that re-forwards runs of an old head, and must not accumulate forever (pruning rules, bounded size).
4. Both existing nudges can fire for one failure: the PR nudge would re-nudge "a failed check" each tick up to NudgeLimit. A new rule must not double-send for the same failure (two ways to do one task) nor silently multiply the NudgeLimit budget.
5. Exactly-once is at-least-once-in-fact (crash between send and save). Comment cursor has the same property; acceptable precedent, must be stated.
6. Executor `Nudges++` branch special-cases ReasonComment only; the sole place a new reason must be handled. Pruning kept-list is the second place a new cache field must be registered. Text fixed and tested; any new text must be a constant in reconcile.go.
7. Escalation: comment nudges never escalate; PR nudges escalate at NudgeLimit. Whether a forwarded failure that the worker never fixes escalates is undecided by precedent.
